newsitem.title: THAILAND: Some 1,000 firms in Thailand face bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Some 1,000 firms in Thailand face bankruptcy.

text.p: About 1,000 Thai firms are expected to face bankruptcy this year and at least 40,000 people could lose their jobs because of a sharp economic slowdown, officials and analysts said on Friday.

Government spokesman Varathep Ratanakorn quoted a National Intelligence Agency (NIA) report as saying that companies most affected would be those involved in textiles, property, and restaurants. No further details were available.
Labour leaders and industry analysts have said at least 40,000 workers in a variety of industries could lose their jobs this year because of a slump in Thai exports.

Labour union leader Chin Taplee said nearly 3,000 workers had already been laid off this year and expected thousands more to lose jobs as more factory owners introduced high technology machinery to replace workers.
Thailand's economy is set to grow at its slowest pace in more than a decade this year at an officially forecast 5.9 percent against 6.4 percent in 1996.
Analysts said the current downturn would deepen social and financial problems and urged the government to find measures to ease the crisis as soon as possible.

Thailand's economy is facing problems on several fronts. The finance and property sectors have been hit by a liquidity crunch and plunging real estate prices, high interest rates have choked businesses, the baht has come under speculative attacks and the stock market has fallen to eight-year lows.

The government has stepped in to streamline the crowded finance sector by promoting mergers between small and medium-sized finance firms, set up a property loan agency to help refinance projects and moved to stabilise the baht on foreign exchange markets.
Varathep quoted NIA chief Bhumarat Taksadipong as telling a cabinet meeting this week that the government needed to find measures to cope with possible massive layoffs in the next six months.
The feared redundancies were expected to affect agricultural and agricultural related industries, Bhumarat said.
Analyst Supavat Saicheua at Krungthai Thanakit Plc told Reuters that small and medium-sized companies were being affected by the slowing economy and the high interest rates.
"I think within the next three or four months some major firms would feel the pinch. Department store sales are a clear indicator in Thailand how well the economy is performing," Supavat said.
Latest figures show department store sales during the first quarter of this year stood at 32.79 billion baht ($1.3 billion), down from 38 billion baht in the same period last year.
Analyst Chetta Meemangkang of Prime Finance and Securities said the unemployment rate was rising and the government should find measures before it was too late.
"Without proper remedy the economy problems will become worse and create more social problems. Right now it's not too late to solve our economic problems," Chetta said.
